North
NōRTH
n. and adj. (rendering Hebrew tsāphōn, Greek borras)
From Old English north, of obscure further origin. The Hebrew tsāphōn is related to a root meaning to hide or lay up in store — the north being the dark quarter, the region the sun never enters, and so the place of what is concealed. Because the great empires that invaded Canaan came down the fertile crescent and entered from the north rather than across the desert, the word acquired a settled prophetic charge: the north is the direction judgment comes from.

Biblical Definition

North in Scripture is the hidden quarter and the quarter of invasion. Job states the cosmology in a line of striking sobriety: “He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing” (Job 26:7) — the northern heavens spread over emptiness, the earth suspended on no support but the will of God. Because Babylon and Assyria descended on Judah from the north, the prophets use the word as a summons: “Then the LORD said unto me, Out of the north an evil shall break forth upon all the inhabitants of the land” (Jer 1:14). Ezekiel's inaugural vision arrives from the same quarter — a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself — so that even the glory of God approaches Judah along the road her enemies use. The north also names a false ambition. In the taunt against the king of Babylon, the sin of the fallen one is put in geographical terms: “I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north” (Isa 14:13). The mountain of assembly in the far north was, in the mythology of the nations, the seat of deity; the boast is a creature's attempt to occupy God's throne-room, and it is answered by yet thou shalt be brought down to hell. Against that stands Zion, which the psalmist calls beautiful for situation, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King — the true mount of assembly, and God's not by seizure.

Webster 1828 Definition

One of the cardinal points of the compass, opposite to the south; in Hebrew the hidden or dark quarter; in the prophets the direction from which invading judgment breaks forth; and the region of the boasted throne of Isaiah 14.

expand to see more

NORTH, n. 1. One of the cardinal points, being that point of the horizon which is directly opposite to the sun in the meridian.

2. Any region or country situated north of another; as the kings of the north.

3. adj. Being in a point toward the north; as the north side, the north gate, the north wind.

4. In Hebrew, the hidden or dark quarter; from a root signifying to hide or lay up, the sun never entering that region.

5. In Scripture, out of the north an evil shall break forth. Jer. 1. The sides of the north. Isaiah 14; Psalm 48.

Key Scripture

Job 26:7 — "He stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing."

Jeremiah 1:14 — "Then the LORD said unto me, Out of the north an evil shall break forth upon all the inhabitants of the land."

Isaiah 14:13 — "For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north:"

Ezekiel 1:4 — "And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire."

Modern Corruption

The mount of the congregation in the sides of the north is treated as proof that Scripture simply absorbed Canaanite myth, and the prophetic north as vaticinium after the fact rather than genuine prediction.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The pressure comes from the historical-critical quarter, in two forms. The first argues that because Ugaritic texts locate a divine assembly on a northern mountain, Isa 14:13 shows Israel's Scriptures borrowing pagan cosmology. But the taunt is put in the mouth of the king of Babylon, and the whole force of the passage is that the boast is a lie which God overturns. Isaiah is not endorsing the mythology; he is quoting a pagan aspiration in order to bury it. That surrounding nations had a mountain-of-the-gods tradition is exactly what one expects if the nations retain corrupted memories of the true God, and Psa 48:2 answers them by locating the real city of the great King.

The second form is the dating argument: since Jeremiah's and Ezekiel's northern-invasion oracles match what Babylon actually did, the passages are assumed to have been composed after the event. This assumes precisely what is in question — that predictive prophecy does not occur. The dictionary holds that God declares the end from the beginning, and that the accuracy of a prophecy is evidence of its inspiration rather than of its late composition. The principle to recover is the one Jeremiah himself was given at his call: the LORD watches over His word to perform it, and He announces judgment beforehand so that it may be recognised as His hand and not as accident when it comes.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew tsāphōn is the north, from a root meaning to hide or store up, the sunless quarter. Greek borras is the north wind and the north. The phrase yark'thē tsāphōn, the sides or uttermost parts of the north, names the mount of assembly.

expand to see more

Hebrew tsāphōn (H6828) — north, the hidden quarter; from tsāphan, to hide, treasure, or lay up in store.

Hebrew yark'thē tsāphōn — the sides, or uttermost parts, of the north; the boasted seat in Isa 14:13 and the true Zion of Psa 48:2.

Hebrew tsāphan (H6845) — to hide or store; thy word have I hid in mine heart (Psa 119:11) uses this root.

Greek borras (G1005) — the north wind, and hence the north quarter; they shall come from the north (Luk 13:29).

Prophetic usage — the invader from the north is Assyria and then Babylon, entering Canaan down the fertile crescent rather than across the eastern desert.

Usage

"Of the created order: he stretcheth out the north over the empty place, and hangeth the earth upon nothing (Job 26:7)."

"Of judgment's direction: out of the north an evil shall break forth upon all the inhabitants of the land (Jer 1:14)."

"Of the creature's boast: I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north (Isa 14:13)."
